'''Jaylen Brown''' (born October 24, 1996) is an American basketball player who recently completed his college career for the [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California Golden Bears]].

==Early life==
Brown attended [[Joseph Wheeler High School]] in [[Marietta, Georgia]].<ref>{{cite web|author=Bob Rathgeber |url=http://www.news-press.com/story/sports/high-school/basketball/2014/12/20/marietta-ga-wheelers-brown-holds-court/20709459/ |title=Marietta (Ga.) Wheeler's Jaylen Brown holds court |website=News-press.com |date=2014-12-21 |accessdate=2016-02-09}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Borzello |first=Jeff |url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/24650170/old-man-jaylen-brown-separates-from-pack----not-just-with-his-game |title='Old man' Jaylen Brown separates from pack - not just with his game |website=CBSSports.com |date= |accessdate=2016-02-09}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author= |url=http://usatodayhss.com/2015/jaylen-brown-wheeler-hoopmixtape-calipari-kentucky-kansas-ucla-georgia-unc-jaylen-brown-roy-williams-visit |title=The Jaylen Brown Blog: No. 2 ranked senior talks UNC visit, SAT, HS season and more | USA Today High School Sports | USA Today High School Sports |website=Usatodayhss.com |date= |accessdate=2016-02-09}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author=Ryan Gorcey |url=http://www.scout.com/college/california/story/1650325-jaylen-brown-in-a-class-of-his-own |title=Cal freshman Jaylen Brown breaks the mold of a five-star, NBA-bound talent; he's as much student as he is athlete |website=Scout.com |date=2016-03-10 |accessdate=2016-03-10}}</ref> As a senior he helped lead his team to a victory in the Georgia AAAAAA state championship. With 0.6 seconds remaining, Brown hit two [[free throws]] to give Wheeler a 59–58 victory.<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=http://usatodayhss.com/2015/jaylen-brown-wheeler-georgia-state-championship |title=Jaylen Brown, No. 7 Wheeler win state title with free throws with 0.6 seconds left | USA Today High School Sports | USA Today High School Sports |website=Usatodayhss.com |date= |accessdate=2016-02-09}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://atlanta.suntimes.com/atl-sports/7/78/101460/jaylen-brown/ |title=Wheeler High's Jaylen Brown wins state title with dramatic free throws |newspaper=Atlanta Sun Times|date= |accessdate=2016-02-09}}</ref>

Brown was rated as a five-star recruit and was ranked by [[Scout.com]] as the best recruit in his class.<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=http://scouthoops.scout.com/player/6131609n-jaylen-brown |title=Jaylen Brown, California SF - Scout |website=Scouthoops.scout.com |date= |accessdate=2016-02-09}}</ref> [[Rivals.com]] and [[ESPN]] both ranked him second behind [[Ben Simmons]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://rivals.yahoo.com/basketballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Jaylen-Brown-133802;_ylt=AtKS8_lqgWvgNZkKQ7X0Xd7VO5B4 |title=Rivals |website=Rivals.yahoo.com |date= |accessdate=2016-02-09}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author= |url=http://espn.go.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/146799/jaylen-brown |title=Jaylen Brown - Basketball Recruiting - Player Profiles - ESPN |website=Espn.go.com |date= |accessdate=2016-02-09}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.masslive.com/hoophallclassic/index.ssf/2015/01/jaylen_brown_scouting_evaluati.html |title=Jaylen Brown scouting: Evaluating No. 2 class of 2015 prospect (VIDEO & PHOTOS) |website=Masslive.com |date=2015-01-19 |accessdate=2016-02-09}}</ref>

==College career==
[[File:20150401 MCDAAG Jaylen Brown dunk (2).JPG|thumb|left|upright|Brown in the [[2015 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2015 McDonald's All-American Game]]]]
Brown was selected to play in the [[2015 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Davis |first=Seth |url=http://www.si.com/college-basketball/2015/01/28/mcdonalds-all-american-game-rosters |title=2015 McDonald's All-American rosters announced |website=SI.com |date=2015-01-28 |accessdate=2016-02-09}}</ref> On May 1, 2015, Brown committed to play for the [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|Golden Bears]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], under coach [[Cuonzo Martin]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/12804453/jaylen-brown-commits-cal-golden-bears |title=Jaylen Brown commits to Cal Golden Bears |website=Espn.go.com |date=2015-05-02 |accessdate=2016-02-09}}</ref> He is listed as a small forward and is heralded as an all-round prospect due to his athleticism.<ref>{{cite web|title = Five-star forward Jaylen Brown commits to Cal for 2015-16|url = http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/25171011/five-star-forward-jaylen-brown-commits-to-cal-for-2015-16|website = CBSSports.com|accessdate = 2015-10-23}}</ref> During his time at California, he managed to attend Master's degree classes as a freshman for the Cultural Studies of Sport in Education.<ref>http://www.mercurynews.com/sports/ci_29104480/cal-freshman-jaylen-brown-making-an-impression-classroom</ref> In addition to that, Brown also managed to learn how to speak Spanish relatively well in his time in California, with him planning on learning three more languages by the age of 25.<ref>http://theundefeated.com/features/jaylen-brown-the-2016-nba-drafts-renaissance-man/</ref>

While playing for California, he managed to provide 14.6 points, 5.4 rebounds, and 2.0 assists with 27.6 minutes played per game in 34 games of action. He managed to provide his best scoring games on November 27, 2015 against [[Richmond Spiders men's basketball|Richmond University]] and January 27, 2016 against [[Utah Utes men's basketball|Utah University]] by recording 27 points in each game. He recorded a season-high 11 rebounds twice during victories on November 23, 2015 against [[Sam Houston State Bearkats men's basketball|Sam Houston State University]] and on [[New Year's Day|January 1]], 2016 against [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado University]]. On January 23, 2016, Brown managed to record a season-high 7 assists to go with 15 points in a close 74-73 victory over [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona University]]. While Brown would prove to be a leading force throughout his only season in California, he would not manage to give the Golden Bears significant success in the NCAA Tournament, providing limited distribution before getting fouled out of the game en route to a loss to #12 seeded [[Hawaii Rainbow Warriors basketball|Hawaii University]], which also resulted in the university's first ever NCAA Tournament victory. However, Brown would also earn All-Pac-12 First Team Honors and be the Pac-12 Freshman of the Year for the production he gave to the Golden Bears all year long.
